findings.summary: Push each runtime into the container's list where it is created, through one attach helper, instead of an index window over the scene's list.
Assign the container's runtime list per addToScene and keep it past the scene's disposal, as the pin keeps its resolved array; drop the dispose-time erase.
Serve flowGraphs as the document's own graph list filled at load, under its own handle kind, instead of aliasing the runtimes.
Refuse a graph's accessors and a runtime's context through property rules stating the pin's fact, and match that refusal in the test.
Require the await where the collection resolver sees through a promise type.
Discard a property read that names no native expression by the empty-cpp rule alone.
Assert the pin's container assignment and runFlowGraphs' attach-and-push; trace the container's count at attach and assert it in the tap check.
Read the keys' nodes from the packaged glTF the executable loads, named by the generated manifest.
Take the tap settle from the registry's reference frame with a short settle for a static camera, and parse the scene argument with Object.hasOwn.
Move the corpus row from staged to scenes and add the exact-manifest row with digests derived the writer's way.
Delete the comment restating the collection table in the compiler and state what the scene 304 gate observes in the registry.
